newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-COLES MYER YEAR SALES UP 5.8 PCT.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-COLES MYER YEAR SALES UP 5.8 PCT.

text.p: Australia's largest retailer Coles Myer Ltd said on Thursday its sales for the three months to July 27 rose six percent to A$4.72 billion and sales for the year to July 27 rose 5.8 percent to A$19.23 billion.
Coles said sales from its food and liquor grouup, including Coles, Bi-Lo, Liquorland and Red Rooster, increased sales by 11.5 percent for the quarter and 11.8 percent for the year.
Comparable Food and Liquor store-on-store sales were up 9.3 percent for the quarter and 8.7 percent for the year.

Coles' General Merchandise group sales, including K-Mart, Officeworks and World-4-Kids, rose 0.2 percent for the quarter and were down 0.1 percent for the full year. Coles did not give store-on-store comparisons for the General Merchandise group.
Total Myer Grace Brothers sales fell 1.9 percent for the quarter and fell 2.3 percent for the year.
Myer Grace Brothers sales adjusted for the redevelopment of the Sydney Grace Brothers store rose 0.6 percent for the quarter and were up 0.9 percent for the year.
Coles Myer chief executive Dennis Eck said he was pleased with the overall result.

"We indicated at our third quarter sales announcement that we expected a similar percentage growth in the second half profit after tax to that experienced in the first half (excluding property disposal profits and abnormals)," Eck said in a statement.
"We maintain that view," he said.
Coles reported a 40.7 percent rise in net profit after abnormals to A$273.6 million for the first half, but the result included a net abnormal gain of A$44.6 million.
First half profits excluding property sales gains and abnormal items rose 23.1 percent.
Food and liquor was now trading 43 percent higher than the base of three years ago and had now recorded 11 consecutive quarters of double-digit sales growth, Coles said.
Kmart's Managing Director Geoff Sadler said in a statement the small fourth quarter sales rise represented the final adjustment to K-Mart's withdrawal from excessive promotions.
"This saw A$25 million in discounted sales passed over," Sadler said.
Officeworks Managing Director Colin Corstorphin said store-on-store sales at the office products group rose 38.3 percent in the year.
"This is giving us the leverage to continue the move into profitability," Corstorphin said.
Eck said overall store-on-store sales from the combined Food and Liquor and General Merchandise stores rose 6.1 percent for the quarter and 5.5 percent for the year.
Coles' Apparel Group, including Target, Katies and Fosseys, increased sales 3.5 percent for the quarter and 2.8 percent for the year.
Target's sales rose 7.1 percent for the quarter and 6.8 percent for the year.
Coles Myers' New Zealand sales fell 19 percent in the fourth quarter to NZ$45 million, while annual sales fell 11.2 percent to NZ$222 million.
Coles' shares were unchanged at A$6.90 by 12.40 p.m. (0240 GMT). -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-18100
